newsitem.title: USA: U.S. citizens warned to use caution in Serbia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. citizens warned to use caution in Serbia.

text.p: The recent arrests of indicted war criminals in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina may spark tensions in the former Yugoslavia, the State Department said in a statement on Thursday, warning Americans to use caution while travelling in Serbia and Montenegro.

"While these arrests have taken place outside of Serbia-Montenegro, the actions could result in heightened sensitivities among the local population, particularly on Serbia's borders with Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia," the department said.

U.S. citizens already in the rump Yugoslav state may contact the U.S. embassy in Belgrade for current security information, the department said. It issued a travel warning on June 5, 1996, warning U.S. citizens not to travel to Bosnia-Herzegovina.

NATO-led forces launched their first concerted attempt to arrest war crimes suspects on Thursday, killing one Bosnian Serb and capturing another in a bold operation approved by President Bill Clinton.

The raid, led by British troops with U.S. logistical support and code-named "Operation Tango," raised expectations that the biggest targets -- Bosnian Serb wartime chief Radovan Karadzic and army commander Ratko Mladic -- might be next.
Peacekeeping officials also expressed concern about the danger of retaliation against their staff on the ground in Bosnian Serb territory.
